articles.title: The role of neurogenic inflammation and CGRP in migraine headache.
articles.abstract: The last 40 years have witnessed a thorough change in our understanding of the mechanisms underlying migraine, initiated by the discovery of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP). A century ago, William Bayliss, Thomas Lewis and other pioneers introduced a visionary neurophysiological mechanism, brought about by peripheral terminals of a specialized subset of primary sensory neurons, which was named 'neurogenic inflammation'; in both mammal and human skin, action potentials generated by injured nerve terminals of primary sensory neurons can invade collateral fibres via antidromic conduction and release a mediator that 'produces the flare and enhances sensitivity of other sensory axons responsible for pain'. This mediator, much later identified as CGRP, provides the missing link between these early observations and modern therapeutic targets. Multiple monoclonal antibodies against CGRP or its receptor along with orally available small molecule antagonists of the CGRP receptor have revolutionized the prevention and acute treatment of migraine. The pharmacokinetic features of anti-CGRP drugs and the paracrine actions of CGRP suggest the proposal that the mechanism underlying migraine headache occurs in a spatially limited microenvironment located outside the blood-brain barrier. According to this hypothesis, the migraine headache milieu comprises CGRP-containing peripheral sensory nerve endings (C-fibre nociceptors) and neighbouring cells, including other nerve fibres (Aδ-fibres), vascular smooth muscle cells and Schwann cells wrapping these nerve fibres.

articles.title: The Hypothalamic Paraventricular Nucleus as an Integrative Hub of Circadian Regulation and a Therapeutic Target in Disease.
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms are endogenous, approximately 24-hour oscillations that align physiology and behavior with the environmental light-dark cycle and support homeostasis. In mammals, the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) serves as the central circadian pacemaker, but its neuronal projections are restricted to a relatively small set of hypothalamic targets. The hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) is an important downstream integrative node that receives direct and indirect temporal signals from the SCN and integrates them with metabolic, visceral, stress-related, and limbic inputs. Through functionally distinct neuroendocrine, autonomic, and central-projecting neuronal populations, the PVN contributes to the temporal regulation of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, glucose metabolism, feeding behavior, nociceptive sensitivity, and cardiovascular function. Cell-type-specific genetic and transcriptomic studies further indicate that PVN neuronal populations exhibit distinct clock-related molecular programs. Studies predominantly in nocturnal rodent models have linked disruption of PVN clocks or rhythmic output to aging-associated decline, metabolic dysfunction, altered tumor immunity, neurodegenerative disease, and pain-related phenotypes. Human post-mortem studies have reported heterogeneous PVN changes in Alzheimer's disease, but direct evidence of PVN clock or SCN-PVN circuit dysfunction in humans remains limited. This review integrates circuit-, cellular-, and molecular-level evidence for the PVN's role in circadian regulation, evaluates interventions spanning timed drug delivery, meal timing, light exposure, and PVN-focused experimental manipulation, and outlines the challenges of translating preclinical findings into clinical practice.

articles.title: Crossing subfamily borders: Mechanosensitive TREK-1 and alkaline-activated TASK-4 form heterodimers with unique functional and pharmacological properties.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The tandem of two-pore-domain potassium (K2P) channels TREK-1 and TASK-4 are expressed in the heart and pancreatic beta-cells. As TREK-1 and TASK-4 belong to distinct subfamilies with different functional hallmarks, heteromerization of these two channels was highly unexpected. However, due to their shared expression in these tissues and their involvement in congenital cardiac arrhythmias, the aim of this study was to probe for a possible formation of TREK-1/TASK-4 heterodimers. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Two-electrode voltage-clamp and inside-out macropatch clamp recordings, together with immunohistochemistry and chemiluminescence-based ELISA assays, were utilized to describe heteromerization of TREK-1 and TASK-4 channels and elucidate the characteristics of this heteromeric channel complex. KEY RESULTS: Here, we show that the mechanosensitive TREK-1 forms heteromeric channel complexes with the alkaline-activated TASK-4. The resulting heterodimers of these only remotely related channels have an enhanced temperature sensitivity, an altered pH dependence and regulation by extracellular sodium. Unlike TREK-1, heteromeric TREK-1/TASK-4 channels are not inhibited via Gs-coupled receptor activation, as the heterodimeric channels are not PKA sensitive. Strikingly, these novel heterodimeric channel complexes are characterized by a unique pharmacology. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: The newly described heterodimerization across different K2P channel families is of major relevance for drugs targeting TASK-4 or TREK-1. Their functional co-expression in different tissues raises the possibility of developing drugs against cardiac arrhythmias and Type 2 diabetes by specifically targeting these unique heterodimeric channel complexes.

articles.title: RETRACTION: Exploring the Antidepressant Potential of Yueju Pill: Insights from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
Clinical Pharmacology in Transgender Medicine: What Gaps Remain?
articles.abstract: Mechanistic information is limited about the effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy and the unique factors that influence the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion properties of medications across therapeutic classes for transgender people. Opportunities exist to address knowledge gaps in transgender medicine using well-designed probe substrate studies, endogenous biomarkers of drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters, and real-world data to identify and address factors that contribute to interindividual variability in drug disposition for transgender people across the life course.

articles.title: Pharmaceutical Industry Pay-Per-Click Advertising Strategies to Influence Public Opinions on Drug Pricing.
articles.abstract: This analysis characterizes the magnitude, timing, and keyword targeting strategies of the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America's (PhRMA) pay-per-click advertising expenditures and their relation to major drug pricing policy developments (2019-2025). Pay-per-click advertising allows advertisers to purchase prominent placement in search engine results, allowing their content to appear above organic results when users search for specific terms. We extracted pay-per-click advertising data from Semrush, a commercial digital marketing intelligence platform, for the domain www.phrma.org from February 2019 through December 2025. We classified keywords into mutually exclusive categories using a specificity-based pattern-matching algorithm and categorized landing-page URLs by content theme using URL string matching. We analyzed monthly spending against a timeline of major legislative and regulatory events. PhRMA spent an estimated $58.8 million across 283,517 keyword instances, generating 17.1 million paid visits to phrma.org and its subdomains. Insurance and health plan keywords dominated spending ($32.4 million; 55.1%), including general and non-health insurance terms. Nearly half of total expenditures (47.5%; $27.9 million) drove traffic to pages classified as criticizing pharmacy benefit managers. Monthly spending showed little linear association with the selected Google Trends index (r = -0.05), but spending surged around well-publicized US legislative and regulatory actions, peaking at $4.8 million in May 2023; March-September 2023 accounted for 36.5% of total spending. Overall, PhRMA pay-per-click spending surges coincided with major US drug pricing policy developments.

articles.title: Validation of senescence as a therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) through navitoclax delivery.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease characterized by steatosis, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Increasing evidence suggests that cellular senescence contributes to MASH progression by promoting lipid accumulation, inflammatory signaling, and fibrogenic responses, highlighting hepatic senescent cells as a potential therapeutic target. Senolytics selectively eliminate senescent cells, but their application in MASH remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed in vitro models integrating hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocyte-macrophage inflammatory crosstalk to facilitate investigation of the contribution of cellular senescence to MASH pathology and to evaluate senescence-targeted interventions. Senescent hepatic cells showed enhanced lipid accumulation and amplified inflammatory signaling with macrophages. Natural Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) derived from adipocytes reduced senescence-associated phenotypes but exhibited context-dependent biological effects, highlighting the limited control over their intrinsic bioactivity. Navitoclax, a senolytic targeting anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins, reduced senescence-associated phenotypes, but its clinical use is limited by its dose-dependent toxicity. Hence, we conceived nano-Cell Vesicle Technology Systems (nCVTs), a biohybrid-based platform combining cell-derived membranes with synthetic lipids for controlled delivery of navitoclax. Navitoclax-loaded nCVTs retained senolytic activity and reduced inflammatory signaling and fibrotic activation in vitro. Importantly, in a Western diet- and fructose-induced (WDF) MASH mouse model, navitoclax-loaded AML-12-derived nCVTs alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation while reducing histopathological activity score and fibrotic profiles. Neither navitoclax formulation reduced platelet counts or hemoglobin concentrations at the tested dose. Collectively, these findings support cellular senescence as a therapeutically relevant target for MASH and identify nCVTs as a promising engineered platform for controlled senolytic delivery.

articles.title: Hydroxytyrosol targets stemness and enhances chemotherapeutic response in 3D metastatic colorectal cancer spheroids.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are increasingly recognized as critical mediators of tumour progression, recurrence and treatment resistance in metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC). Hydroxytyrosol, a phenolic compound derived from virgin olive oil, has shown promising anticancer activity against CRC cells. However, its effects on cancer stemness and its potential to enhance the efficacy of conventional chemotherapy drugs remain largely unexplored. PURPOSE: To assess whether hydroxytyrosol suppresses CSC-associated traits and improves chemotherapy response using a 3D spheroid model established from the metastatic CRC cell line LoVo. METHODS: LoVo spheroids were generated under stirred-tank culture conditions and characterized by molecular and functional assays. Hydroxytyrosol effects on LoVo spheroids were assessed using cell viability, ALDH activity, clonogenic and RT-qPCR assays. Drug combination interactions were determined using the Chou-Talalay method. RESULTS: LoVo spheroids recapitulated key tumour features, including a hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal phenotype, enhanced stemness, high clonogenic capacity, and localized hypoxia. Hydroxytyrosol reduced cell proliferation in a dose-dependent manner, with LoVo spheroids exhibiting greater resistance than 2D cultures (IC50: 1454 µM vs 91 µM). Hydroxytyrosol significantly decreased ALDH activity at 125-500 µM (39-57%) and clonogenic potential at 1-100 µM (21-84%). It also significantly affected the expression of markers associated with the proliferation (CDKN1A), epithelial-mesenchymal transition (VIM), Wnt/β-catenin (AXIN2) and stemness (CD44, CD133 and LGR5). In combination studies, hydroxytyrosol showed strong synergistic interactions with the chemotherapy drug irinotecan (Combination Index: 0.07-0.15). Similar effects were observed in CSC-enriched HT29 spheroids. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence that hydroxytyrosol targets CRC CSC-associated phenotypes and synergistically enhances irinotecan efficacy in metastatic CRC spheroids. These findings position hydroxytyrosol as a promising adjuvant strategy to counteract CSC-associated drug resistance and sensitize metastatic CRC cells to chemotherapy, supporting its further evaluation as a chemosensitising agent in advanced CRC.

articles.title: Biogenic gold nanoparticles in breast cancer nanomedicine: sustainable synthesis, multifunctional engineering, and the road to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: The use of plant, algal, microbial or biomolecule based reducing and capping agents to synthesize gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) has paved the way for the use of these materials as versatile candidates for breast-cancer nanomedicine. In addition to being a more sustainable synthetic pathway, the biological elements attached to the surface of AuNP can have an impact on the formation process, the stability of AuNP in solution, the interaction with cells and the therapeutic activity of the particles. This review critically assesses the recent advances of biogenic AuNPs for application in breast cancer, ranging from direct phytogenic anticancer formulations, engineered drug delivery system, HER2 associated biosensing platform, photoresponsive therapies, and multimodal theranostic constructs. Preclinical reported mechanisms are increased cellular uptake, increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, increased DNA damage, cell-cycle arrest, and apoptosis. Additionally, Biogenic AuNPs offer flexible surfaces for the conjugation of chemotherapeutics, phytochemicals, nucleic acids, antibodies, photosensitizers and tumour-targeting ligands, thus providing opportunities for subtype-specific strategies for HER2-positive disease and triple-negative breast cancer. Currently however, in vitro studies dominate the evidence base, and many of these studies make use of limited models of cell lines. Although the bioinorganic nature of Biogenic AuNPs is scientifically interesting, their clinical applicability will rely on the development of reproducible synthesis procedures, characterization in biological environments, validation for the respective sub-type, quantitative biodistribution and clinically representative preclinical models.

articles.title: Interpreting liver volume changes after rifampicin in healthy volunteers.
articles.abstract: Rifampicin-associated liver volume changes in healthy volunteers provide an opportunity to examine the human relevance of xenobiotic-induced liver growth. This Comment considers three aspects of the clinical analysis relevant to interpreting the observed response. Clarification of whether the volumetric outcomes and choice of normalisation were prespecified, alongside paired treatment effects and confidence intervals, would help establish the basis for inference and assess the response's magnitude and precision. For a small volumetric response, blinded repeat segmentation of existing magnetic resonance images and details of scan timing and pre-scan intake would help assess reproducibility under comparable physiological conditions. Associations between 4β-hydroxycholesterol and liver volume could also be examined using within-participant rifampicin-minus-placebo differences, with appropriate attention to the crossover design and an exploratory interpretation. Most of these suggestions could be addressed through protocol information and existing imaging and crossover data, strengthening interpretation of the human findings and guiding further investigation of pregnane X receptor-mediated liver growth.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of intra-articular triamcinolone acetonide in arthritis treatment: a two-decade FAERS and JADER study with machine learning prediction and SHAP-based interpretation.
articles.abstract: Triamcinolone acetonide (TA) is a widely used glucocorticoid for inflammatory diseases, including arthritis. Although intra-articular TA injection provides effective symptom relief, its safety profile in real-world clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. Adverse event reports associated with intra-articular TA injection for arthritis were retrieved from the FAERS database (2004-Q1 2026) and the JADER database (2004-Q4 2025). Disproportionality analyses were performed using four signal detection algorithms, including ROR, PRR, BCPNN, and MGPS. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate signal heterogeneity and robustness. Time-to-onset patterns were assessed using Weibull analysis. Endocrine-related adverse events were further evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and machine learning classification models with SHAP-based interpretation. A total of 738 FAERS reports involving intra-articular TA were identified, covering 27 system organ classes. Multiple established and potential safety signals were detected, including adrenal insufficiency, hyperglycemia, osteonecrosis, bacterial arthritis, postmenopausal hemorrhage, and Cushing's syndrome. Additional potential safety signals included type 2 diabetes mellitus, flushing, erythema multiforme, pemphigus, and septic shock. The strongest disproportionality signals were observed for injection site calcification, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis suppression, injection site atrophy, and Cushing's syndrome. Most adverse events occurred within 30 days after exposure (84.55%), with a median onset time of 5 days (IQR: 2-14). External signal consistency assessment using 112 JADER reports identified eight signals consistent with FAERS findings. Multivariable logistic regression showed that age, sex, therapy type, and reporter type were associated with endocrine-related adverse event reporting. Machine learning models demonstrated good classification performance, with random forest achieving the highest test set AUC (0.864). SHAP analysis identified demographic and treatment-related variables as important contributors to model classification. This study provides a comprehensive real-world pharmacovigilance assessment of intra-articular TA and identifies both established and potential safety signals. Integration of conventional signal detection, regression analysis, and interpretable machine learning approaches may facilitate systematic characterization of TA-associated adverse event patterns and support future safety monitoring.

articles.title: Lycopene-loaded albumin nanoparticles developed by an ultrasound-driven assembly-emulsification method for parenteral nutrition.
articles.abstract: Intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD), a severe complication of parenteral nutrition (PN), remains difficult to prevent and treat. We hypothesized that the bioactive carotenoid lycopene could alleviate hepatocellular signaling disturbances involved in its pathogenesis. However, IFALD patients require intravenous nutrient administration; therefore, potential lycopene treatment would necessitate an appropriate delivery system to overcome its poor water solubility. In this study, we evaluated the biological activity of free lycopene in THLE-2 hepatocytes under IFALD-like conditions and developed lycopene-loaded human serum albumin nanoparticles (Lyc@AlbNPs) for PN supplementation. Lycopene attenuated MAPK- and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling and modulated the expression of genes involved in cholesterol metabolism, including ABCA1, CYP7A1, and SREBF2. Lyc@AlbNPs were prepared by adding lycopene directly to the albumin solution rather than first dissolving it in an organic solvent, as required in typical methods for producing albumin nanoparticles. Initial lycopene-albumin assemblies formed during bath sonication; subsequent ultrasonic emulsification promoted their reorganization into smaller particles, yielding Lyc@AlbNPs with a mean size of 72.2 ± 3.1 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.265 ± 0.013, and lycopene loading of 9.42 ± 0.22 %. Thermal and diffraction analyses indicated disruption of the crystalline structure of lycopene during initial assembly formation. Lyc@AlbNPs were nonhemolytic and cytocompatible in THLE-2 cells. Five ready-to-use three-chamber PN bags were supplemented with Lyc@AlbNPs to assess potential interactions; all admixtures met the predefined compatibility criteria and remained stable for 24 h. These findings indicate that free lycopene modulates inflammatory and metabolism-related signaling in an in vitro IFALD model, while the albumin-based nanoformulation enables its addition to PN admixtures. The study also demonstrates an alternative formulation approach to incorporating poorly soluble compounds into albumin nanoparticles.

articles.title: Development of plant-derived polyphenols-loaded protein films for topical application.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop gelatin/sodium caseinate films containing quercetin or rutin and to evaluate their physicochemical, antioxidant, and in vitro release properties for potential topical application. Films were prepared at a gelatin-to-sodium caseinate mass ratio of 1:0.5, with glycerol at 30% and either flavonoid (quercetin or rutin) at 1%, 3%, or 5% (w/w, relative to the total protein mass). SEM revealed irregular surfaces and crystal-like domains within the matrix. No new bands or pronounced shifts were observed in the ATR-FTIR spectra, possibly suggesting the lack of new covalent bonds forming between the flavonoids and the protein matrix. However, noncovalent interactions cannot be excluded. Opacity increased with flavonoid loading, whereas moisture content, solubility, and swelling ratio were only slightly affected, possibly due to low nominal flavonoid loading and limited aqueous solubility. Water vapor permeability and mechanical properties showed limited changes: relative to the unloaded film, water vapor permeability increased, and tensile strength decreased significantly only at 5% rutin, while elongation at break increased significantly only at 1% rutin. The pronounced DPPH radical-scavenging activity of both flavonoids was largely retained after incorporation, remaining high at all loadings (82.46 ± 1.38%-85.20 ± 1.29%). Cumulative release from the 5% quercetin and 5% rutin films reached 52.67 ± 3.05% after 300 min and 53.91 ± 3.04% after 450 min, respectively. The first-order model provided the best fit for both release profiles. These findings support further development of gelatin/sodium caseinate films as potential prolonged-release carriers for topical flavonoid delivery.

articles.title: Huashi Runzao Decoction alleviates ferroptosis in salivary gland epithelial cells through RBM15B-associated m6A regulation in Sjögren's disease.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huashi Runzao Decoction (HSRZD) is a well established herbal formula developed for the clinical management of Sjögren's disease (SjD). Previous randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that HSRZD improves salivary gland function and reduces disease activity in patients with SjD. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of HSRZD against salivary gland dysfunction in Sjögren's disease (SjD) and to explore the mechanisms underlying m6A mediated regulation of salivary gland injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical profile of HSRZD was characterized by UHPLC-MS/MS. NOD/ShiLtJ mice and IFN-γ-stimulated primary human salivary gland epithelial cells (SGECs) were used to evaluate the protective effects of HSRZD against SjD associated salivary gland dysfunction and ferroptotic injury. Dysregulated m6A regulators were screened and identified as potential mediators involved in SjD pathogenesis and HSRZD treatment. RNA-seq, gene silencing, RIP-qPCR, mRNA stability assays, and MeRIP-qPCR were performed to elucidate the role of the RBM15B mediated m6A regulatory pathway in regulating GPX4 mRNA stability and ferroptosis in SGECs. RESULTS: A total of 118 chemical constituents were identified in the HSRZD aqueous decoction. In NOD/ShiLtJ mice, HSRZD improved salivary gland function, suppressed ferroptosis in SMG tissues, and restored RBM15B expression, while RBM15B was markedly downregulated in primary SGECs from patients with SjD. RBM15B silencing promoted ferroptosis in SGECs and altered the expression of ferroptosis-related genes, with GPX4 showing the most pronounced reduction. RBM15B silencing decreased GPX4 expression and reduced its mRNA stability. Furthermore, RBM15B silencing reduced m6A enrichment within the GPX4 mRNA region containing the predicted m6A motif at nucleotide 727. In IFN-γ-stimulated SGECs, HSRZD attenuated ferroptosis and restored RBM15B and GPX4 expression, whereas these protective effects were partially abolished by RBM15B silencing. CONCLUSIONS: HSRZD alleviates salivary gland dysfunction in SjD by restoring RBM15B expression and enhancing GPX4 mediated ferroptosis resistance in SGECs. The RBM15B-GPX4 axis may represent an m6A associated mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of HSRZD in SjD. However, the interactions between HSRZD constituents and RBM15B, and the functional role of the candidate GPX4 m6A site, require further experimental validation.

articles.title: Hinokitiol alleviates liver fibrosis in rats: Plausible role of hepatic stellate cell activation and TGF-β/Smad2/3 axis.
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis represents a progressive pathological condition with excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, primarily driven by hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation and sustained inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. Despite its clinical burden, effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of hinokitiol (HKT), a natural tropolone derivative, in attenuating liver fibrosis using both in vitro and in vivo models. Human LX-2 HSCs were employed to assess the mechanistic effects of HKT under TGF-β-induced fibrogenic conditions. HKT treatment significantly suppressed myofibroblastic transdifferentiation, as evidenced by downregulation of α-SMA, N-cadherin, vimentin, and collagen I, and reduced HSC migration. Additionally, HKT attenuated reactive oxygen species generation via inhibition of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) expression. In an experimental model of alcohol- and carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced liver fibrosis, oral administration of HKT (2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg) significantly ameliorated hepatic injury, as indicated by reduced serum ALT and AST levels, improved liver morphology, and restored hepatic architecture. Histopathological and biochemical analyses revealed a pronounced reduction in collagen deposition, hydroxyproline content, and fibrotic bridging. Mechanistically, HKT suppressed the TGF-β/Smad2/3 cascade, thereby inhibiting HSCs activation and ECM accumulation. Furthermore, HKT reduced the expression of lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2) protein, which further impeded the stiffening of fibrous liver. In addition, HKT mitigated hepatic oxidative stress, while concurrently attenuating pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β. Taken together, our findings establish HKT as a potential candidate to limit fibrosis progression and hepatic tissue remodeling by impeding HSCs activation and the TGF-β/Smad2/3/LOXL2 cascade.

articles.title: Paternal Preconception EGCG Exposure is Associated with Reduced Heart Weight, Altered Cardiac Morphology, and Changed Cardiac CREG1/ERK1/2 Levels in Adult Female Mouse Offspring.
articles.abstract: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), the major bioactive polyphenol in green tea, exhibits broad bioactivities. Existing research has uncovered diverse regulatory effects of EGCG on cardiac tissue. Nevertheless, whether paternal preconception EGCG exposure reshapes cardiac structural characteristics in offspring remains largely uncharacterized. In the present work, adult male C57BL/6J mice received 10 mg/kg/day EGCG via drinking water over a 60-day preconception period prior to mating. We observed that paternal EGCG treatment coincided with lower heart weight and heart-to-body weight ratios in adult female offspring, while no comparable shifts were detected in male littermates. Subsequent fluorescent TUNEL and WGA staining revealed unaltered cardiomyocyte apoptosis in female offspring, yet the cross-sectional area of ventricular cardiomyocytes was substantially diminished. This reduced cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area may have contributed to the decreased heart weight, and this structural phenotype was associated with upregulated cellular repressor of E1A-stimulated genes 1 (CREG1) protein abundance and attenuated extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) phosphorylation in cardiac tissue. Collectively, these observations suggest that paternal preconception EGCG exposure is associated with reduced cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area and reduced heart weight selectively in adult female mouse offspring.

articles.title: β-elemene suppressed EMT via IGF1R inhibition in osimertinib treated AXL low-expressing EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: β-elemene (β-ELE) is the principal active component of Elemene, and its anti-NSCLC effect is relatively moderate. However, it shows promising potential in synergistically enhancing the efficacy of chemotherapeutic agents. Osimertinib (OSI) is a third EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor that selectively inhibits mutant EGFR. However, OSI lacks cross-inhibitory activity against IGF1R and tends to induce compensatory activation of IGF1R signaling, which is a key factor contributing to OSI tolerance in AXL-low-expression NSCLC cells. Therefore, combining OSI with IGF1R inhibitors is a promising regimen for improving therapeutic efficacy. Based on preliminary screening, we found that β-ELE exhibits binding affinity and inhibitory activity toward IGF1R. It notably increased the anticancer effect of OSI both in vitro and in vivo in AXL-low expression EGFR mutant NSCLC. Mechanistically, β-ELE combined with OSI attenuated OSI induced activation of IGF1R, promoting the inhibition of cancer cell proliferation and EMT, which could be partially abolished by IGF1R overexpression. RNA-seq analysis revealed that AREG is a key downregulated gene transcriptionally regulated by IGF1R in β-ELE + OSI treated cells. β-ELE + OSI induced EMT inhibition was reversed by IGF1R overexpression, but could be restored via AREG knockdown in IGF1R overexpressed NSCLC cells. Furthermore, β-ELE + OSI increased the binding between IGF1R and amphiregulin (AREG), promoting IGF1R nuclear translocation, which were both observed in vitro and in vivo. Altogether, β-ELE promotes the efficacy of OSI via suppressing IGF1R/AREG-mediated EMT in OSI treated NSCLC cells, supporting the co-administration of β-ELE and OSI as a novel integrative strategy for NSCLC treatment.

articles.title: 13β,21-dihydroeurycomanone induces pyroptosis in lung adenocarcinoma cells via activating RIG-1/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway.
articles.abstract: Pyroptosis, an inflammatory and lytic form of programmed cell death, has emerged as a promising therapeutic platform for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) treatment. The role of 13β,21-dihydroeurycomanone (DHEN), a quassinoid isolated from the root extract of Eurycoma longifolia, in pyroptosis induction of LUAD cells remains unclear. Here, we found that DHEN significantly inhibited the proliferation of A549 and NCI-H1975 cells, two LUAD cell lines, but had no obvious cytotoxic effects on normal human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). Animal experiments further revealed that DHEN inhibited the growth of human LUAD xenograft tumors in nude mice with no obvious systemic toxicity to healthy mice. Morphologically, DHEN induced pyroptosis-like morphological changes in LUAD cells. Correspondingly, DHEN inhibited the expression of Pro-Caspase-1 and gasdermin D (GSDMD) proteins , and promoted the expression of Cleaved-Caspase-1, Cleaved-N-terminal GSDMD (GSDMD-N), NLRP3, and NLRC4 proteins, accompanied with concomitant increase of Caspase-1 activity, interleukin (IL)1β and IL18 mRNA expression, and IL1β and IL18 secretion in LUAD cells. As expected, VX-765, a specific pyroptotic inhibitor, significantly abrogated DHEN-induced proliferation inhibition, GSDMD cleavage, and IL1β and IL18 secretion. Mechanically, DHEN up-regulated RIG-1 expression, while RIG-1 knockout significantly abrogated DHEN-induced proliferation inhibition, pyroptosis-like morphology changes, Pro-Caspase-1 and GSDMD protein cleavage, NLRP3 protein expression, Caspase-1 activation, and IL1β and IL18 secretion in LUAD cells. Taken together, our results indicate that DHEN exhibits its anti-tumor activity in LUAD cells by inducing pyroptosis through activating the RIG-1/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway, thus highlighting DHEN as a potential chemotherapeutic agent with low toxicity for LUAD treatment.

articles.title: Investigating the Toxicological Effects of 3-Phenoxybenzoic Acid Exposure on Sarcopenia via Integrated Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, and In Vitro Validation.
articles.abstract: 3-Phenoxybenzoic acid (3-PBA), a widespread degradation product of pyrethroid insecticides, poses potential health risks, but its mechanistic role in sarcopenia remains unclear. We integrated network toxicology, machine learning using LASSO, Elastic Net, random forest, and SVM-RFE, SHAP analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro validation to investigate its underlying effects. A total of 119 candidate genes were prioritized, and five candidate hub genes (GOT2, HDAC4, NDUFS3, ORAI1, and PLIN3) were identified. Enrichment analyses indicated associations with energy metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, muscle contraction, oxidative stress-related processes, and mitochondrial function. Molecular docking and MD simulations supported the plausibility of interactions between 3-PBA and selected hub proteins, while revealing distinct dynamic behaviors among the simulated complexes. In differentiating C2C12 cells, 3-PBA suppressed cell viability, increased Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression, decreased Myog mRNA expression, and altered the transcript levels of the five candidate hub genes. Further functional assays and MYOM3 immunofluorescence analysis showed decreased intracellular ATP levels, increased intracellular Ca2+ levels, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and an overall reduction in MYOM3-positive fluorescence and MYOM3-positive myotube-like structures following 3-PBA exposure. These findings suggest that 3-PBA exposure is associated with disturbances in cellular energy status and Ca2+ homeostasis, oxidative injury, and altered myogenic structural characteristics, providing experimental support for its potential adverse effects on skeletal muscle cells and its possible relationship with sarcopenia.

articles.title: Col23a1 acts as an ECM-resident signal to drive DDR1-p38/ERK-dependent EMT in antimony-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Antimony (Sb) exposure causes pulmonary fibrosis, but the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Using a chronic Sb exposure mouse model combined with single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified Col23a1 as a highly and specifically expressed collagen in alveolar epithelial type II (AEC II) cells, with its expression correlating with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Further analysis demonstrated that Col23a1 was enriched in the extracellular matrix (ECM), where it engaged discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) to activate p38 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation, thereby driving EMT in AECs. Protein-protein interaction screening identified P4HA1 as a Col23a1-interacting candidate and that molecular docking supported a potential interaction. Functionally, P4HA1 stabilized Col23a1 and promoted its ECM deposition, while DDR1-p38/ERK signaling reciprocally sustained P4HA1 expression, forming a self-amplifying positive feedback loop. Pharmacological inhibition of DDR1 or p38/ERK and P4HA1 knockdown each attenuated Sb-induced EMT in AECs. Importantly, AEC-specific Col23a1 knockdown via AAV6-SPC-shCol23a1 in mice substantially reduced fibrotic remodeling and EMT in vivo, and ECM from Col23a1-knockdown lungs failed to induce EMT in naïve epithelial cells, confirming that ECM-resident Col23a1 is the functional component driving this fibrotic signal. Collectively, these findings establish a Col23a1-DDR1-p38/ERK self-amplifying axis as a driver of Sb-induced pulmonary fibrosis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the pulmonary toxicity of Sb and identifying this axis as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Molecular Descriptor-Based QSAR Modeling of Carbamate Derivatives for Predicting Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitory Activity.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibition remains an important therapeutic strategy for symptomatic treatment of Alzheimer's disease. Quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling may help identify molecular features associated with AChE inhibitory activity. METHODS: Forty-one carbamate derivatives with reported AChE inhibitory activities were analyzed using 1,420 DRAGON molecular descriptors. An 11-descriptor multiple linear regression model was developed using forward stepwise selection and evaluated through leave-one-out cross-validation, Y-randomization, applicability-domain analysis, nested cross-validation, and external validation. RESULTS: The model showed good fit to the training data (R2 = 0.9207), adjusted (R2= 0.8907), (RMSE = 0.0766) and leave-one-out performance (Q2LOO = 0.8382), RMSECV = 0.1094). Y-randomization yielded an empirical probability of 0.0190 for obtaining a training (R2) at least as high as the observed value. However, supplementary nested cross-validation produced a mean out-of-fold (R2) of 0.178, while external validation yielded (R2ext = -0.0548), indicating limited generalizability. The selected descriptors represented electronic, topological, geometrical, and molecular-property characteristics. CONCLUSIONS: The model identifies descriptor-activity associations within the studied carbamate series but has limited demonstrated external predictive capability. It should therefore be considered an exploratory QSAR model requiring further validation on larger, independent datasets before application to the design or prioritization of new AChE inhibitors.

articles.title: D(+)-Raffinose Pentahydrate Induces Senescence in Glioblastoma Cells by Upregulating P21 Expression.
articles.abstract: D(+)-Raffinose pentahydrate (RP), a naturally derived galacto-oligosaccharide, has emerged as a low-toxicity compound with substantial antitumor potential. However, its therapeutic effects on glioblastoma (GBM) remain largely unexplored. Here, our study demonstrated that RP significantly reduced GBM cell s proliferation in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in a subcutaneous xenograft model in vivo, despite its inability to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Notably, RP also suppressed the growth of human primary glioblastoma tumor cells. Through comprehensive RNA-seq analysis, molecular docking calculations and flow cytometry, we identified P21 as an important mediator of the cellular response to RP treatment, with cellular senescence serving as the key cytotoxic mechanism. Genetic manipulation experiments confirmed that P21 deficiency attenuated the inhibitory effects of RP, whereas P21 overexpression enhanced its antitumor activity. Mechanistically, RP induced G1 cell cycle arrest through p21-associated regulation, ultimately triggering cellular senescence and exerting anticancer effects on GBM. These findings not only elucidate the antitumor mechanisms of RP but also highlight its potential as a novel therapeutic agent for GBM treatment.

articles.title: Network Medicine Identifies a FOSL1/SNAI1-CCND1/CXCR4 Network Associated with N-Methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine-Related Gastric Precancerous Lesions and Modulated by Apigenin.
articles.abstract: N-Methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG) is a direct-acting alkylating carcinogen. We investigated how MNNG-associated gene networks relate to gastric precancerous lesions (GPL) and gastric cancer (GC), and whether apigenin modulates selected network components. Public stage-resolved transcriptomes were integrated with co-expression analysis, protein-interaction topology, toxicant-associated gene mapping, network proximity, and machine-learning feature selection. Public expression and survival resources informed prioritization; clinical gastric-tissue transcriptomics and MNNG-exposed GES-1 cell transcriptomics/proteomics provided separate expression evidence. Intervention experiments used 10 μM MNNG for 48 h with 10 or 20 μM apigenin in cells, and 200 mg/L MNNG for 20 weeks with 15 or 30 mg/kg/day apigenin during weeks 9-20 in rats. The analyses identified an expression-associated network involving GDF15, TGFB1, FOSL1, SNAI1, CCND1, CXCR4 and PLAU, with inflammatory, proliferative and matrix-remodeling programs. Clinical and cellular evidence varied by cohort and assay. Apigenin was prioritized using its negative proximity Z-score (-2.166), short network distance (1.069), and biological plausibility. It counter-regulated selected MNNG-associated expression changes, particularly involving FOSL1, SNAI1, CCND1 and CXCR4. Docking and 50-ns molecular dynamics simulations provided supportive computational evidence for candidate structural hypotheses. Together, the findings nominate an apigenin-responsive network associated with MNNG-related gastric molecular alterations and prioritize its components for subsequent functional investigation.

articles.title: Reversal of acquired osimertinib resistance by YAP inhibition in lung cancer is associated with lipid metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Osimertinib (Osi), as the third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI), has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, recent studies have found that its acquired resistance severely limits its therapeutic effect. This study shows that YAP activation is associated with lipid metabolic reprogramming in Osi-acquired resistance, providing new insights into overcoming this clinical challenge. In H1975/OR cells, YAP phosphorylation was decreased and nuclear translocation was increased, indicating YAP activation. Inhibition or knockdown of YAP significantly re-stored Osi sensitivity. YAP upregulated the expression of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), fatty acid synthase (FASN), and stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD1), and promoted the synthesis of triglycerides, cholesterol, and phospholipids. Lipidomics revealed that YAP inhibition reduced multiple phospholipids. Furthermore, inhibition of YAP downregulated the anti-apoptotic protein B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL2) and enhanced Osi-induced apoptosis. This study firstly links YAP activation to lipid metabolic reprogramming and reveals its crucial role in Osi-acquired resistance. These findings not only deepen the understanding of the EGFR-TKI resistance mechanism but also provide a new therapeutic strategy for clinically overcoming Osi-acquired resistance. Targeting the phospholipid synthesis pathway mediated by YAP may effectively reverse the acquired resistance of NSCLC to Osi.

articles.title: Dermal permeation of representative small molecule nitrosamines: Implications for risk assessment.
articles.abstract: Small-molecule nitrosamines (SMNs) are potent carcinogenic impurities that have been detected in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, drinking water, and other environmental sources. Although regulatory risk assessments are primarily based on systemic exposure following oral intake, quantitative information regarding dermal absorption of these compounds remains limited. The dermal permeation of five representative SMNs (NDMA, NMBA, NPYR, NDEA, and NDIPA) was investigated across intact and tape-stripped human cadaver skin using Franz diffusion cells under occluded infinite-dose conditions. Steady-state permeability coefficients were determined and correlated with log POct/water. An experimentally derived permeability relationship was externally validated using N-nitroso-desethyl lidocaine (NDL), a representative nitrosamine drug substance-related impurity. All nitrosamines permeated intact human skin with experimentally determined permeability coefficients ranging from 1.90 × 10⁻⁷ to 3.02 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s. Excluding NDMA, permeability demonstrated a stronger positive linear relationship with lipophilicity (R² = 0.766). Despite its extreme hydrophilicity, NDMA exhibited substantially greater permeability than expected. The experimentally derived correlation successfully predicted the permeability of N-nitroso-desethyl lidocaine within approximately 1.5-fold of the experimentally observed value. Barrier disruption significantly increased cumulative permeation of all compounds, with enhancement decreasing progressively as lipophilicity increased. Finally, we incorporated experimentally determined permeability coefficients into a steady-state screening framework to estimate the theoretical skin exposure area required to reach FDA's lifetime acceptable intake (AI) values. This study establishes experimentally determined dermal permeability coefficients for representative regulatory small nitrosamines, validates a predictive relationship applicable to structurally related compounds, demonstrates the influence of barrier integrity on dermal transport, and introduces a permeability-based steady-state screening framework for dermal risk assessment of nitrosamine impurities in topical products.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of free and nanodrugs on the chicken embryo model via different routes.
articles.abstract: The chicken embryo has emerged as a useful in vivo model for evaluating drug delivery strategies; however, the influence of inoculation route on toxicity and pharmacokinetics remains poorly explored. This study investigated the effects of different inoculation routes on the toxicity and pharmacokinetics of free and nanoencapsulated norfloxacin, indomethacin, and lidocaine in chicken embryos. On embryonic day 10, formulations were administered via the shell membrane, allantois, chorioallantoic membrane, or amniotic cavity. Toxicity was evaluated after six days based on mortality, embryo weight, and histological alterations in the liver and kidney. Pharmacokinetic parameters of commercial and nanoformulated norfloxacin were determined in serum and allantoic fluid after administration through the same routes. Norfloxacin did not affect embryo weight, whereas lidocaine increased it and indomethacin reduced it. Histological alterations occurred only after amniotic administration of nanoformulations, including renal inflammatory or degenerative changes and hepatic degeneration. Nanoencapsulated norfloxacin achieved higher and delayed serum maximum concentrations than the commercial formulation across most routes, while higher concentrations of the commercial formulation were detected in allantoic fluid. These findings demonstrate that the route of inoculation plays a critical role in determining the pharmacokinetic behavior and toxicity of free and nanoencapsulated formulations, providing practical guidance for designing pharmacokinetic and toxicological studies using the chicken embryo model.

articles.title: P2Y6R is associated with adipose inflammation and muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer cachexia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer has one of the highest incidences of cancer-associated cachexia, a multi-organ wasting syndrome driven by complex tumor-host interactions. Although adipose tissue functions as an active endocrine organ contributing to systemic inflammation, the mechanisms linking adipose inflammation to skeletal muscle wasting remain incompletely understood. METHODS: An orthotopic pancreatic tumor mouse model was combined with pharmacological P2Y6R inhibition using MRS2578. Cachexia-associated targets were identified by transcriptomic analysis of mouse datasets, and P2Y6R function was examined in vitro cancer-associated adipocyte (CAA) and C2C12 myotube models. RESULTS: Transcriptomic analysis identified P2Y6R as a cachexia-associated gene, with expression selectively upregulated in visceral adipose tissue and CAAs under pancreatic cancer conditions. In contrast, P2Y6R expression was minimal in skeletal muscle and comparatively low in tumor tissue. In the orthotopic model, pharmacological inhibition of P2Y6R with MRS2578, initiated before overt weight loss, attenuated body weight loss. This was accompanied by reduced serum IL-6 and IL-1β levels (IL-1β at 3 mg/kg only) and decreased expression of the atrogenes mRNA expression in skeletal muscle. In vitro, conditioned medium from CAAs suppressed myotube differentiation, whereas P2ry6 knockdown in adipocytes attenuated this effect. Mechanistically, the P2Y6R-dependent secretome of cancer-associated adipocytes was associated with increased atrogene expression and altered FOXO3 phosphorylation in myotubes. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that P2Y6R is associated with adipose inflammation and muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer cachexia, and that pharmacological P2Y6R inhibition attenuates cachexia progression in a preventive setting. These results suggest a potential contribution of adipocyte P2Y6R to adipose-muscle crosstalk and highlight P2Y6R as a candidate therapeutic target for cancer-associated muscle loss.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, in silico Studies, and Biological Evaluation of N4-Acetyl/Benzoyl Piperazinyl Ciprofloxacin-Amino Acid Conjugates as Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Agents.
articles.abstract: This study reports a second-stage optimization of our previously reported ciprofloxacin derivatives through molecular hybridization, with structural modifications aimed at improving antimicrobial potency and activity against resistant strains. Their structures and identities were confirmed by spectroscopic techniques, elemental analysis, and HPLC. In vitro antimicrobial activity showed enhanced potency across a panel of bacterial strains. The derivatives demonstrated promising activity against both wild-type and resistant strains, while the most active derivatives also exhibited promising antimycobacterial activity. The most active compounds were selected for further in vitro and live-cell mode-of-action studies. Several compounds showed biofilm-inhibiting activity against Staphylococcus aureus at sub-MIC. Phenotypic mode-of-action studies indicated topoisomerase inhibition in both Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis. Enzyme inhibition studies revealed potent activity against DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Additionally, the best anti-Helicobacter pylori candidates showed promising urease inhibition. Selected derivatives showed bactericidal activity with minimal resistance development compared with ciprofloxacin. The cytotoxicity study indicated low in vitro cytotoxicity under the tested conditions. Molecular modeling supported favorable binding and inhibitory potential, while QSAR linked physicochemical properties to biological activity, providing mechanistic insights and guiding compound optimization toward improved efficacy and development. Overall, the synthesized ciprofloxacin hybrids showed promising antimicrobial activity and potential to combat bacterial resistance.

articles.title: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and pharmacokinetics of remibrutinib, an oral, highly selective Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor, in healthy participants at steady state.
articles.abstract: Remibrutinib (LOU064), an oral, highly selective Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is approved in the United States, China, European Union, and Japan for treating adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria who remain symptomatic despite treatment with H1-antihistamines. This study characterized the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of remibrutinib in healthy participants to evaluate its pharmacokinetics, mass balance, and metabolite profile following oral and intravenous administration. Five participants received oral [14C]remibrutinib (100 mg) and 2 received an intravenous microdose of [14C]remibrutinib (100 μg) as a 2-mL bolus at steady state, alongside unlabeled remibrutinib. Remibrutinib showed fast absorption (time to reach maximum concentration: 0.5 hours, oral; 1.13-1.33 hours, intravenous), with fraction absorbed estimated at 75%-88%. Elimination half-life was 3.29 hours (oral), 1.85 hours (intravenous arm A), and 2.06 hours (intravenous arm B). Total radioactivity exposure area under the curve extrapolated to infinity in whole blood was 85% (oral arm) and >90% (intravenous arms) of that in plasma, indicating no preferential distribution to red blood cells, and total radioactivity remained detectable up to 600 hours, indicating extensive distribution (apparent volume of distribution: 576-2120 L). Remibrutinib was mainly metabolized at the acrylamide moiety (glutathione conjugation and dihydrodiol formation via an epoxide intermediate) and by amide hydrolysis. Predominant circulating metabolites were M68a/b diastereomers, with none exceeding 10% of the total drug-related material. Excretion was predominantly through feces, accounting for 31.8% of the dose after oral and ∼69.5% after intravenous administration. Mass balance was incomplete following oral dosing (56.2%) but nearly complete after intravenous dosing (96.8%-97.2%). Remibrutinib was well tolerated. In conclusion, this study comprehensively characterized the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion profile of remibrutinib in humans. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: At steady state, oral [14C]remibrutinib showed fast absorption and good systemic availability, with extensive metabolism after oral and intravenous dosing. Mass balance was incomplete after oral but complete after intravenous dosing. Radioactivity was predominantly excreted in feces (31.8% and ∼69.5% after oral and intravenous dosing, respectively). No circulating metabolite exceeded 10% of total radioactivity. The main fecal metabolite was M24, representing 7.22% and 16.9% of the dose following oral and intravenous dosing, respectively. Remibrutinib was well tolerated in healthy participants.

articles.title: Allosteric modulator of dopamine transporter inhibits cocaine-induced behaviors in rats.
articles.abstract: Psychostimulant use disorders, particularly cocaine use disorder, is marked by compulsive drug seeking and high relapse rates. Cocaine blocks the dopamine transporter (DAT), preventing dopamine (DA) reuptake, leading to elevated DA signaling-a key driver of its addictive properties. Although behavioral interventions such as contingency management have demonstrated efficacy in treating stimulant use disorders, their long-term effectiveness and accessibility remain limited, and no US Food and Drug Administration-approved pharmacotherapy for psychostimulant use disorder currently exists, highlighting the need for novel treatment options. We investigated the therapeutic potential of KM822, a novel allosteric DAT modulator that binds to a distinct domain different from the cocaine/DA binding site. When infused into the nucleus accumbens, KM822 significantly attenuated cocaine-induced hyperlocomotion of an intracranial dose of 25 μg cocaine, with no significant effect observed at higher cocaine doses tested. To assess the impact of KM822 on cocaine's rewarding properties, we used the conditioned place preference (CPP) test. KM822 pretreatment during conditioning successfully blocked the development of cocaine-induced CPP. To model relapse, we evaluated cocaine-primed reinstatement in the CPP assay and found that KM822 pretreatment before cocaine priming effectively blocked reinstatement behavior. Importantly, KM822 alone did not produce preference in the CPP test, suggesting that KM822 has low abuse potential. At the protein level, KM822 alone did not significantly alter c-Fos expression, a marker of neuronal activation, but attenuated cocaine-induced c-Fos expression. Together, these findings demonstrate that KM822 can inhibit cocaine-related behaviors and neural responses and serve as a proof of concept for the therapeutic potential of allosterically targeting DAT. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This project provides proof of concept that targeting the dopamine transporter allosteric site with modulators such as KM822 offers a promising strategy for developing pharmacotherapies for psychostimulant use disorder, especially cocaine use disorder.

articles.title: Polymeric microparticles for local treatment of cutaneous leishmaniasis: a comparison of drug delivery systems and unmet clinical needs.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) remains a significant therapeutic challenge, particularly in New World settings, where current local treatments are limited by pain, repeated administration, poor drug penetration, species-dependent efficacy, and systemic toxicity. There is an unmet need for short, safe, effective, and field-adapted therapies. AREAS COVERED: This article reviews current local treatment strategies for CL and examines advances in drug-delivery systems, with particular emphasis on polymeric microparticles. Attention is given to biodegradable PLGA microparticles as long-acting intralesional depots. Preclinical evidence and clinical data are evaluated alongside key barriers to implementation. EXPERT OPINION: Polymeric microparticles, especially PLGA-based depots, represent a promising strategy to modernize local CL treatment by sustaining therapeutic drug concentrations at the lesion while minimizing systemic exposure and reducing dosing frequency. Future development should prioritize species-specific clinical trials, standardized outcomes, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic optimization, patient-centered measures, cost-effectiveness, and particularly scalable manufacturing. If current translational efforts are successful, single-dose therapies could become a realistic component of CL management within the next few years.

articles.title: Nanoparticle-Mediated Therapies for Atherosclerosis: A Novel Approach to Targeted Treatment.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Atherosclerosis(AS) remains a leading cause of global cardiovascular mortality due to the formation of lipid rich plaques and chronic vascular inflammation. Conventional therapies, including statins, antiplatelet agents and surgical interventions, primarily control risk factors by preventing new plaque deposits but show limited ability to selectively target inflamed vascular sites. OBJECTIVE: This review critically evaluates current advances in nanoparticle mediated drug delivery for atherosclerosis, with emphasis on mechanistic targeting of inflamed plaques, modulation of macrophage driven inflammatory and oxidative pathways within the diseased vascular microenvironment. This review also highlights comparative analysis of major nanoparticle systems, integration of theranostic functionalities for simultaneous molecular imaging and therapy. The translational barriers are also addressed to enable clinical implementation.Significance of Review: Despite advancements in lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory drugs, current atherosclerosis treatments are limited by inadequate plaque specificity, rapid systemic clearance, off-target toxicity, and persistent cardiovascular risk. Nanoparticle based systems can solve these problems with simultaneous diagnosis and therapy, thereby addressing major unmet clinical needs.Key Findings: Different types of nanoparticles demonstrate promising therapeutic outcomes by modulating macrophage activity, reducing oxidative stress, enabling controlled drug release and improving plaque imaging. Theranostic nanoparticles further allow simultaneous diagnosis and treatment. However, large-scale manufacturing, nanotoxicology and regulatory constraints continue to hinder clinical translation. CONCLUSIONS: Nanoparticle-mediated therapies represent a transformative approach for atherosclerosis by enabling precision, targeted and multifunctional treatment. Continued optimization of safety, scalability and regulatory compliance will be essential for successful clinical adoption and improved patient outcomes.

articles.title: Network Pharmacology and In Vivo Validation Reveal the Potential Protective Mechanisms of Chonggu Granules in Knee Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disorder characterized by progressive cartilage loss, chronic low-grade inflammation, and oxidative injury. Ferroptosis-associated iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation have been implicated in osteoarthritic cartilage damage. This study investigated the protective effects and potential multi-target mechanisms of Chonggu Granules (CGG) in KOA. METHODS: Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to identify candidate CGG compounds, targets, and pathways. KOA was induced in rats by intra-articular papain injection. Rats were randomly allocated to the Control, Model, glucosamine hydrochloride (AT), CGG, Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), and CGG plus ML385 groups. Cartilage histopathology, mitochondrial ultrastructure, chondrocyte apoptosis, oxidative stress, serum Fe2+ levels, lipid peroxidation, inflammatory cytokines, and the expression of Nrf2 and related antioxidant and ferroptosis-associated molecules were evaluated. RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified 115 overlapping CGG-KOA targets, including the hub target NFE2L2, enriched in pathways related to inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding between several major CGG compounds and multiple hub targets. In vivo, CGG attenuated cartilage degeneration, mitochondrial abnormalities, chondrocyte apoptosis, inflammatory cytokine production, oxidative stress, elevated serum Fe2+ levels, and lipid peroxidation. CGG also partially normalized the expression of Nrf2, HO-1, GPX4, and other ferroptosis-associated molecules. These effects were partially attenuated by ML385. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that CGG exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against KOA-related cartilage injury by modulating inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis-associated processes. The partial attenuation of these effects by ML385 supports the involvement of Nrf2-associated antioxidant signaling and downstream ferroptosis-related responses. CONCLUSION: CGG alleviated KOA-related cartilage injury and ferroptosis-associated oxidative damage through potential multi-target regulation, with Nrf2-associated antioxidant responses contributing to these protective effects.

articles.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking on the Mechanism of Epimedium in the Treatment of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To investigate the mechanism of Epimedium in the treatment of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) using network pharmacology and molecular docking approaches. METHODS: The active components and corresponding targets of Epimedium were screened from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology (TCMSP) database. COPD-related disease targets were obtained from the OMIM and GeneCards databases. All target genes were standardized using the UniProt database. Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) networks, Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analyses were performed using the ClusterProfiler R package and the STRING database. The herb-compound-target network and the target-pathway network were constructed in Cytoscape to identify core compounds, key targets, and major pathways. Finally, molecular docking between the core targets and the active compounds was performed using AutoDock Vina. RESULTS: A total of 23 active components and 223 corresponding targets of Epimedium were identified in the treatment of COPD. The core targets included TP53, IL1B, AKT1, TNF, and IL6. GO enrichment analysis indicated that biological processes were primarily enriched in responses to lipopolysaccharide, molecules of bacterial origin, epithelial cell proliferation and injury repair, and regulation of apoptotic signaling pathways. KEGG pathway enrichment yielded 200 signaling pathways; after excluding irrelevant pathways, the most significantly enriched pathways were predominantly associated with inflammation and immune regulation, including the PI3KAkt, TNF, IL-17, AGE-RAGE, and p53 signaling pathways. Molecular docking results demonstrated that the active compounds of Epimedium exhibited favorable binding affinities with IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that Epimedium exerts therapeutic effects against COPD through a multicomponent, multi-target, and multi-pathway regulatory mechanism. The integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses indicate that modulation of inflammatory and oxidative stress-related pathways may represent the principal molecular basis underlying its pharmacological activity, providing mechanistic support for future experimental validation. CONCLUSION: Epimedium exhibits the multi-component, multi-target, and multi-pathway characteristics of traditional Chinese medicine. Its therapeutic effects in COPD are mediated through active ingredients such as quercetin, kaempferol, and luteolin, which regulate core targets including IL-1β, IL-6, TNF, and TP53, and modulate inflammation- and immune-related pathways such as PI3K-Akt, AGE-RAGE, and IL-17. These actions collectively contribute to anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative stress effects, regulation of pulmonary apoptosis, and inhibition of pulmonary vascular and airway remodeling. This study tried to apply network pharmacology and molecular docking to elucidate the multi-target synergistic mechanism of Epimedium in the treatment of COPD, providing a theoretical basis for subsequent experimental validation and drug development.

articles.title: Hesperidin Enhances Doxorubicin Cytotoxicity in MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells: Evidence from Cellular, Gene Expression, Global DNA Methylation, and Molecular Docking Analyses.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Doxorubicin efficacy in breast cancer is constrained by chemoresistance and toxicity. Hesperidin, a citrus flavonoid, exhibits anticancer and epigenetic regulatory properties. This study evaluated whether hesperidin enhances doxorubicin cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells and characterized the associated apoptotic and Heat-Shock (HSP60, HSP90) transcripts, as well as global DNA methylation. METHODS: Cytotoxicity and synergy were assessed using the MTT assay and the Chou-Talalay method (CI). Apoptosis and cell cycle were analyzed by flow cytometry. Expression of BAX, BCL2, HSP60, and HSP90 was quantified using RT-qPCR. Global DNA methylation (5-mC%) was assessed colorimetrically, alongside molecular docking simulations for HSP60 and HSP90. RESULTS: Combining hesperidin with doxorubicin produced synergistic cytotoxicity (CI < 1) and a dosereduction index of 1.95 for doxorubicin. The combination induced apoptosis, accompanied by upregulation of BAX, downregulation of BCL2, and modulation of HSP60/HSP90 transcript levels. Additionally, the combination attenuated doxorubicin-induced global hypermethylation. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding affinities of hesperidin toward both HSP60 and HSP90, particularly HSP60; however, these findings remain correlative without proving direct target engagement. DISCUSSION: The synergistic response, paired with modulated apoptotic markers and global DNA methylation, suggests that hesperidin sensitizes MCF-7 cells to doxorubicin through multi-targeted cellular and epigenetic pathways. While docking and transcriptomic shifts indicate potential chaperone involvement, these preliminary observations require further functional validation. CONCLUSION: Hesperidin enhances doxorubicin cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells by modulating apoptosis, stressresponse transcripts, and DNA methylation. These in-vitro findings support further mechanistic and in-vivo evaluation of this combination strategy.

articles.title: Rivastigmine and Emerging Nanotechnological Strategies for Targeted Delivery: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease affects millions of people globally; it is an irreversible and incurable disease, characterized by gradual cognitive decline as well as pathophysiological changes including the presence of senile plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. There are several risk factors associated with Alzheimer's disease, including elevated blood pressure, blood sugar concentration, alcohol consumption, smoking, and sleep disturbances. Rivastigmine is an FDA-approved cholinesterase inhibitor used to treat Alzheimer's disease. It is available as oral solutions, capsules, and transdermal patches. Oral administration can lead to detrimental and off-target effects such as nausea and vomiting, and the use of patches can cause irritation and rashes. Across various systems, including the Cardiovascular (CVS), Gastrointestinal (GI), immunological, dermatological, and respiratory systems, rivastigmine has been associated with effects that further necessitate targeted drug delivery. Novel drug delivery systems such as Liposomes, Polymeric Nanoparticles, Dendrimers, Solid Lipid Nanoparticles (SLNs), Nanostructured Lipid Carriers (NLCs), nano-emulsions, and Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles (MSNs) have been developed to address the limitations of conventional dosage forms. These new formulations possess the ability to increase drug loading capacity, enhance penetration across the BBB, reduce expulsion, and offer controlled release of the drug. As a result, rivastigmine can be targeted to the intended site, with fewer off-target effects. However, formulation-specific toxicity may still occur. Positive off-target effects, such as improved appetite, protection against malnutrition, and evidence of advantage in treating colitis, were also observed with rivastigmine. However, detailed studies of its mechanism of action are needed to provide a scientifically sound justification for repurposing rivastigmine. Google Scholar and PubMed were searched for literature for this review and included studies that met the criteria.

articles.title: In silico Design and Molecular Modeling of Piperazine-Oxadiazole Appended Imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]Thiadiazoles as Promising RTK Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cancer remains a significant global health issue, and the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) is a key therapeutic target in various cancer types. This study aimed to identify new, potent EGFR inhibitors. METHODS: In silico analysis was used to design and evaluate novel Imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole derivatives with dual pharmacophores. Molecular docking was performed using Autodock Vina 1.1.2 to assess their binding affinities to EGFR Kinase, VEGFR2, and Human HER2. Pharmacological profiling was also conducted to predict ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) and drug-likeness properties. To confirm the stability of the most promising candidates, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations were performed using Maestro. RESULTS: The docking analysis revealed that all ligands exhibited favorable binding affinities toward the selected receptor tyrosine kinases (1YWN, 3POZ, and 3PP0), with binding energies ranging from -8.3 to -10.4 kcal/mol. Among the targets, 3POZ showed the strongest overall ligand interactions. Notably, Ligand 6c showed superior binding affinity with a maximum docking score of -10.4 kcal/mol (Pose 1). ADMET profiles of all the compounds showed that compounds showed drug likeness in the order of 6a > 6b > 6c as per the Lipinski Rule of Five. DISCUSSION: The designed imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole derivatives exhibited stable binding within the EGFR kinase domain, with supportive comparative analysis against VEGFR2 and HER2. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations confirmed favorable interaction stability. ADMET profiling suggested acceptable drug-likeness and oral absorption. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed scaffolds as promising RTK inhibitors warranting further experimental validation. CONCLUSION: This study employed molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET profiling to evaluate substituted imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole derivatives (6a-6c) targeting VEGFR2, EGFR, and HER2. Among the series, the nitro-substituted compound 6c exhibited the strongest binding affinity and most stable interactions within the kinase active sites. Molecular dynamics results confirmed stable complex formation, as evidenced by consistent RMSD and persistent hydrogen bonding. ADMET analysis indicated favorable drug-likeness and predicted oral bioavailability. Overall, compound 6c emerges as the most promising candidate for further experimental validation as a receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

articles.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
articles.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.

articles.title: Case Studies on the Safety Assessment Strategy for Botanical Extracts in Cosmetic Products.
articles.abstract: The safety assessment of botanical extracts has been the subject of extensive discussion due to the inherent challenges posed by their complex mixtures of unknown components, variations related to the raw materials and manufacturing processes, and differences arising from the plant parts and origins. These factors make safety evaluations more complicated compared to those of well-characterized chemicals. This study presents three representative botanical extracts to illustrate practical tiered approaches for assessing their safety in cosmetic products. Mauritia flexuosa fruit oil, classified as a food-derived material, allows for the waiver of systemic toxicity assessment based on its established history of safe use. Hydrolyzed Myrtus communis leaf extract is sufficiently characterized to enable a component-based risk characterization. In contrast, Chrysanthemum parthenium (feverfew) extract lacks comprehensive toxicological data and adequate chemical characterization; therefore, a weight-of-evidence approach is applied, integrating multiple lines of evidence to support safety conclusions. These case studies demonstrate the applicability of tiered assessment strategies and decision-tree approaches for botanical extracts in cosmetic safety evaluations.

articles.title: Efinaconazole-Loaded Liposomal Nanocarriers: A Box-Behnken Design Approach in Formulation Designing and Optimization for Onychomycosis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To design, optimize, and evaluate efinaconazole-loaded liposomal formulation with sustained drug release, enhanced trans-ungual drug penetration, and improved drug retention for treatment of onychomycosis. SIGNIFICANCE: Conventional topical therapies for onychomycosis are limited by poor nail permeability and low drug retention. The optimized liposomal nanocarrier system enhances trans-ungual drug penetration with sustains release kinetics showing potential for effective drug delivery and patient compliance. METHODS: Liposomes encapsulating efinaconazole were synthesized via the ethanol injection technique. A Box-Behnken design was employed for optimization using Design Expert® software. The independent variables included phospholipid (HSPC), cholesterol, and stirring speed, while dependent variables were particle size, PDI, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, and cumulative drug release. The optimized liposomes underwent comprehensive characterization including in vitro drug release, TEM, DSC, release kinetics, ex vivo nail permeation, and physical stability. RESULTS: The optimized formulation prepared with HSPC:cholesterol (4.83:1 w/w ratio) exhibited particle size of 190 nm, PDI of 0.187, zeta potential of -28.20 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 47.80%. It showed sustained release profile with 75.41% cumulative drug release at 12 h following Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetic model. TEM analysis confirmed spherical, nanosized, unilamellar vesicles, and the DSC indicated successful drug encapsulation. The ex vivo drug permeation across human nail plate showed approximately 1.7-fold higher permeation of liposomal formulation compared to pure drug solution. CONCLUSION: The optimized liposomal formulation closely matched the software-predicted values and demonstrated enhanced trans-ungual drug penetration, sustained drug release, and satisfactory physical stability, indicating its promising prospects as transungual drug delivery system.
